description: Classifies email by direct-to-recipient status, category, action requirement, and urgency. See README.md for the complete processing flow.

direct_to_you.instructions: Was this message written specifically to the recipient as a direct personal or professional communication? A platform-relayed direct message may qualify. General thread comments, repository activity, list posts, campaigns, digests, and system notifications do not qualify merely because a human authored some underlying content.

criteria.yes: A person is directly addressing the recipient in a personal or professional communication.
criteria.no: Not specifically addressed to the recipient, including automated notices, general GitHub activity or thread comments, mailing-list posts, newsletters, campaigns, and system-generated messages.

category.instructions: Classify into exactly one category. HARD RULES: if direct_to_you is yes, category must be personal or work. Email_lists requires explicit mailing-list evidence such as a List-ID header or a known list sender or recipient address; social-network digests and notification emails are not email lists.

criteria.personal: Personal life, family, friends, finances, home, travel, purchases, health, appointments, memberships, clubs, community organizations, household services, and recurring personal activities. Includes legitimate automated member notices and event reminders from organizations with an existing personal relationship. Excludes unsolicited bulk social-network digests and trending-post notifications.
criteria.work: Professional or technical correspondence, conferences, recruiters, colleagues, business, or industry matters tied to the recipient’s professional relationships or responsibilities. Excludes recurring author-led broadcast letters or essays that are not specifically about the recipient, even when they discuss technology, work, or business.
criteria.github: Notifications delivered by GitHub about repositories, issues, pull requests, commits, reviews, or discussions.
criteria.email_lists: A genuine discussion mailing list where members converse, supported by an explicit List-ID header or a known mailing-list sender or recipient address. Excludes Nextdoor, LinkedIn, Facebook, forum digests, social-network updates, and ordinary notification emails.
criteria.newsletters: Recurring author-led broadcast letters or essays clearly written in the personal voice of an identifiable individual, primarily intended to be read. They feel like a person writing to an audience in a friend-like or conversational way and remain newsletters even when discussing technology, work, or business. Excludes company-branded publications, institutional bulletins, corporate editorial content, product content, marketing, platform-generated digests, and direct one-to-one email.
criteria.subscriptions: Recurring account-based digests, recommendations, activity summaries, and content roundups from social networks, community platforms, forums, or feed-driven services. Examples include Reddit digests, Nextdoor neighborhood summaries, and similar platform-generated content. Excludes direct personal messages, genuine discussion mailing lists, editorial publications, and promotion-first marketing.
criteria.potential_spam: Legitimate or plausibly legitimate but unwanted bulk acquisition or promotion: unsolicited marketing, discounts, product updates, cold sales, recruiting blasts, unclear bulk outreach, company-branded publications, corporate editorial content, and branded content marketing. Do not use for informational notices or event reminders from an existing personal membership or service unless the message is primarily promotional.
criteria.spam: Clearly deceptive, fraudulent, malicious, or worthless junk. Includes phishing, fake invoices, fabricated accounts or rewards, random-domain casino offers, fake dating messages, adult bait, miracle-cure claims, impersonation, and similar scam patterns.

needs_action.instructions: Only email categorized as personal or work can require action. For every other category, choose no. For personal or work, decide whether the recipient has a legitimate reason or obligation to act; ignore actions serving only the sender’s marketing, sales, or fraudulent goal.

criteria.yes: The category is personal or work, and a reply is genuinely expected or the recipient must decide, pay, schedule, provide information, review assigned work, meet a deadline, or resolve a legitimate account or security issue.
criteria.no: The category is not personal or work, or the message is informational or optional. Includes advertisements, promotions, discounts, newsletters, subscriptions, product announcements, GitHub notifications, email lists, scams, phishing, unsubscribe links, and generic calls to click, buy, register, deposit, claim, or learn more.

urgency.instructions: Assign urgency independently of whether action is required. HARD RULE: spam and potential_spam are always urgency_3; ignore fabricated scarcity, threats, and promotional deadlines.

criteria.urgency_1: Highest: a legitimate message needs attention today, someone is blocked, or a real deadline or security risk is within 24 hours.
criteria.urgency_2: Medium: a legitimate message deserves attention within several days.
criteria.urgency_3: Lowest: no immediate legitimate time pressure; informational, optional, spam, potential spam, marketing, or fabricated urgency.
